mainTopic: Who gets the hides of קרבנות: sources for the כהנים' share, and what happens when an offering becomes פסול before or after flaying
overview: This amud is about who gets the hides of קרבנות. A ברייתא teaches that the כהנים get the hide of an עולה, and asks how we know they also get the hides of all קדשי קדשים. The first opinion learns it from the extra words 'אשר הקריב' and limits it to קדשי קדשים. רבי ישמעאל learns it from a קל וחומר, and רבי says no proof is needed, because the hide always follows the meat. Only the עולה, which is skinned and burned, needs a פסוק for its hide, and a טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים and an אונן get no share. The גמרא then explains how each opinion uses the words of the פסוק, including רבי ישמעאל's גזירה שוה about the bones of the עולה. A new משנה rules that a hide goes to the כהנים only if the offering became פסול after flaying. It also records רבי עקיבא and the חכמים arguing about a בכור found to be a טריפה. Finally, the גמרא asks whether the two משניות follow רבי or רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. אביי and רבא give opposite answers, and רבא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Priests get the hide even when the עולה did not count for its owner
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes an earlier point. The כהנים get the hide of a valid עולה in every case, even if it did not count for the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the כהנים should not get its hide? The פסוק says 'the hide of the עולה', which means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא wraps up a point it started on the previous amud. It asks whether the כהנים lose the hide of an עולה that did not count for its owner, and answers no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that if the עולה did not do its job for the owner, the כהנים lose their share. The פסוק says 'עור העולה' with no conditions, so as long as the קרבן itself is valid, the hide goes to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, with no conditions

phrases.english: Should the priests not be entitled to its hide?
phrases.notes: 'Its' points back to the עולה discussed just before this, one that was valid but did not count for its owner.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'The hide of the burnt offering', in any case.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:8

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יְהוּ כֹּהֲנִים זַכָּאִין בְּעוֹרָהּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a derivation that began before this section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים get the hide of a valid עולה even if it did not count for its owner.

steps.title: How do we know about the hides of other most-holy offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא points out that the פסוק only mentions the עולה, and asks where we learn that the כהנים also get the hides of other קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The hide of the עולה': this only teaches me about the hide of an עולה. Where do we learn about the hides of all קדשי קדשים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens a new question. The פסוק only mentions the עולה, so what about the hides of other most-holy קרבנות like a חטאת or אשם?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the פסוק covers only one type of קרבן. The ברייתא wants a source that widens the rule to the whole group of קדשי קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: I only have (the פסוק only teaches)
Offerings of the most holy level

phrases.aramaic: ״עוֹר הָעֹלָה״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עוֹר הָעוֹלָה,
phrases.english: 'The hide of the burnt offering': I have only the hide of the burnt offering.
From where do we know about the hides of the offerings of the most sacred order?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עוֹר הָעוֹלָה, עוֹרוֹת קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of an עולה to the wider group of קדשי קדשים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that the כהנים get the hides of all קדשי קדשים, not only of the עולה.

steps.title: The extra words 'which he offered' widen the rule
steps.stepSummary: The words 'אשר הקריב' (which he offered) teach that the rule covers other קרבנות too, not just the עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'the hide of the עולה which he offered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by pointing to the extra words at the end of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'the hide of the עולה'. Adding 'which he offered' widens the rule to the hides of other קרבנות that the כהן brings.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'The hide of the burnt offering which he has offered.'
phrases.notes: The added words 'which he offered' are what widen the rule to other offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: עוֹר הָעֹלָה אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'אשר הקריב' extend the hide rule beyond the עולה.

steps.title: Maybe this includes even lesser-holy offerings
steps.stepSummary: If the words widen the rule, maybe they widen it too far and include קדשים קלים as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps I should include even קדשים קלים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא worries that the extra words prove too much. Maybe now even the lesser-holy קרבנות give their hides to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Which he offered' sounds like it could cover every קרבן. The ברייתא needs to set a limit on how far this extra wording reaches.

phrases.english: One might have thought that I include
even offerings of lesser sanctity?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reach of the source given in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general phrase like 'which he offered' could include every קרבן, even קדשים קלים.

steps.title: The word 'עולה' limits the rule to most-holy offerings
steps.stepSummary: Because the פסוק still names the עולה, the rule only covers קרבנות like the עולה, meaning קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'עולה'. Just as an עולה is קדשי קדשים, so too the rule covers all קדשי קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the worry. The word 'עולה' sets the limit: only קרבנות at the same holiness level as the עולה are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two parts of the פסוק work together. 'Which he offered' widens the rule, and 'עולה' keeps it to the עולה's level, which is קדשי קדשים. So קדשים קלים are left out.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this first opinion, the כהנים get the hides of all קדשי קדשים but not of קדשים קלים. 'Which he offered' widens the rule, and 'עולה' sets its limit.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'Burnt offering',
just as a burnt offering is of the most sacred order,
so too all offerings of the most sacred order.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר עֹלָה – מָה עוֹלָה קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים, אַף כֹּל קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the widening through a comparison to the named case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra words include every קרבן, even קדשים קלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only קדשי קדשים are included, since they match the עולה's level of holiness.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל asks the same question
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל begins a different approach by asking the same question: where do we learn about the hides of other קדשי קדשים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: 'The hide of the עולה' teaches only about the עולה. Where do we learn about the hides of קדשי קדשים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now brings רבי ישמעאל, who asks the same question again. This sets up a different way of answering it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is the same as in step 2, but רבי ישמעאל will not learn the answer from the extra words of the פסוק. He is about to answer it with logic instead.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
'The hide of the burnt offering': I have only the burnt offering.
From where do we know about the hides of the offerings of the most sacred order?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: עוֹר הָעֹלָה – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא הָעוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the question of step 2 in order to give a different answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for the hides of all קדשי קדשים, according to רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the עולה
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים get the hide of an עולה even though they get none of its meat. So surely they get the hides of קדשי קדשים, whose meat they do eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: It can be learned with logic. If with an עולה, whose meat the כהנים do not get, they still get its hide, then with קדשי קדשים, whose meat they do get, isn't it logical that they get the hide?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers with a קל וחומר, reasoning from the weaker case to the stronger case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עולה is the weaker case, since the כהנים get none of its meat, and still they get its hide. A חטאת or אשם is a stronger case, since the כהנים eat its meat. So they should surely get its hide too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical (it can be learned by reasoning)
Reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger case

phrases.english: And it is a logical inference:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה עוֹלָה, שֶׁלֹּא זָכוּ בִּבְשָׂרָהּ – זָכוּ בְּעוֹרָהּ;
phrases.english: Just as with a burnt offering, whose meat they do not acquire, they acquire its hide,
with offerings of the most sacred order, whose meat they do acquire,
is it not logical that they acquire their hides?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִין הוּא: וּמָה עוֹלָה, שֶׁלֹּא זָכוּ בִּבְשָׂרָהּ – זָכוּ בְּעוֹרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ישמעאל's question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר: getting the meat is a stronger connection than lacking it, so getting the hide follows.

steps.title: The altar disproves the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The מזבח gets the meat of an עולה but not its hide, so getting the meat does not have to mean getting the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the מזבח prove otherwise: it gets the meat but does not get the hide!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא attacks the קל וחומר with a counterexample from the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed that whoever gets the meat surely gets the hide. The מזבח breaks that rule: all the meat of an עולה is burned on it, yet the hide goes to the כהנים.

phrases.english: Let the altar prove otherwise,
as it acquires the meat and does not acquire the hide!
phrases.notes: The עולה's meat all goes up on the altar, but its hide goes to the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִזְבֵּחַ יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that getting the meat leads to getting the hide.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מזבח gets the meat of an עולה but not its hide, so the link between meat and hide does not hold.

steps.title: The altar never gets hides, but the כהנים get some
steps.stepSummary: The מזבח is different because it never gets any hide at all. The כהנים already get some hides, so the מזבח is no proof for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about the מזבח? It does not get any hides at all. Can you compare it to the כהנים, who do get some hides?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back against the counterexample by showing that the מזבח is not a fair comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח has no share in hides at all, so of course it does not get them. The כהנים already have a share in hides, from the עולה, so the מזבח cannot teach us anything about them.

keyTerms.meaning: What about this case? It is special because...

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְמִזְבֵּחַ – שֶׁכֵּן לֹא זָכָה בְּמִקְצָת;
phrases.english: What is notable about the altar? It does not acquire hides in any case.
phrases.notes: Literally, 'it does not acquire some', meaning the altar gets no hides at all, not even some.

phrases.english: Will you say the same about the priests, who acquire some?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְמִזְבֵּחַ – שֶׁכֵּן לֹא זָכָה בְּמִקְצָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counterexample of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the counterexample is a different kind of case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מזבח shows that getting the meat does not lead to getting the hide.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מזבח never has any share in hides, unlike the כהנים, so it proves nothing about them.

steps.title: Since they get some hides, they get them all
steps.stepSummary: Because the כהנים get some hides, from the עולה, they get the hides of all קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they get some hides, they get all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes רבי ישמעאל's reasoning with a final conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the כהנים have a share in hides, there is no reason to limit it to the עולה. Their right extends to all קדשי קדשים, which are the stronger case.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions agree that the כהנים get the hides of all קדשי קדשים. The first learns it from the words of the פסוק, and רבי ישמעאל learns it from a קל וחומר that holds up against the challenge from the מזבח.

phrases.english: Since they acquire some, they acquire all.
phrases.notes: 'All' here means the hides of all קדשי קדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְזָכוּ בְּמִקְצָת, זָכוּ בְּכוּלֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion after the defense in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי ישמעאל, the כהנים get the hides of all קדשי קדשים, learned from a קל וחומר.

steps.title: The hide always goes with the meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the פסוק is needed only for the hide of the עולה, because everywhere else the hide follows the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: We only needed the פסוק for the hide of the עולה. In every other case, the hide goes wherever the meat goes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a different and simpler approach. He says there is no need to prove that the כהנים get the hides of קדשי קדשים at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל worked hard to learn the hides of קדשי קדשים from the עולה. רבי says that work is not needed. There is a general rule that the hide follows the meat, so whoever gets the meat gets the hide. The only case that needs a פסוק is the עולה, because its meat goes to the מזבח but its hide goes to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: the hide follows the meat; whoever gets the meat gets the hide

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that the hide follows the meat, explains the hide in almost every קרבן. That leaves the עולה as the one special case.

phrases.english: Rabbi says:
We did not need it at all
phrases.notes: Literally 'all of it we did not need.' He means the פסוק is not needed to teach about the other hides.

phrases.english: except for the hide of the burnt offering alone.
For in every case
the hide follows the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עַצְמוֹ לֹא הוּצְרַכְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a simpler approach than רבי ישמעאל's argument in steps 6-10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hide goes to whoever gets the meat. A פסוק is needed only for the hide of the עולה.

steps.title: Examples showing the hide goes with the meat
steps.stepSummary: Burned פרים and שעירים are burned with their hides. In a חטאת, an אשם and communal שלמים, the כהן gets both meat and hide. In קדשים קלים, the owners get both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bulls and goats that are burned are burned together with their hides. A חטאת, an אשם and communal שלמים are a gift to the כהן: he may skin them, or eat the meat with the hide still on. קדשים קלים belong to the owners: they may skin them, or eat the meat with the hide still on.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי, still speaking in the ברייתא, goes through the different kinds of קרבנות to show that his rule is true. In each case, whoever gets the meat also gets the hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three examples. When the meat is burned, the hide is burned too. When the meat goes to the כהן, the hide is his too. When the meat goes to the owners, the hide is theirs too. Since the hide always follows the meat, these cases need no separate פסוק for the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: bulls that are burned outside the camp, not eaten
goats that are burned outside the camp
communal שלמים, eaten by the כהנים
קרבנות of lesser holiness, eaten by the owners
the owners who brought the קרבן

phrases.english: Bulls that are burned and goats that are burned:
they and their hides are burned together.
A sin offering, a guilt offering, and communal peace offerings
are a gift to the priest;
if they want, they skin them,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא רָצוּ – אוֹכְלִין אוֹתָן עַל גַּבֵּי עוֹרָן.
phrases.english: if they don't want to, they eat them on their hide.
Offerings of lesser holiness go to the owners;
if they want, they skin them,

phrases.aramaic: רָצוּ – אוֹכְלִין אוֹתָן עַל גַּב עוֹרָן.
phrases.english: if they want, they eat them on their hide.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִין וּשְׂעִירִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples that support רבי's rule from step 11
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the hide follows the meat
steps.raayaSupportSource: The laws of burned קרבנות, of קרבנות eaten by כהנים, and of קדשים קלים

steps.title: The עולה is skinned, so it is different
steps.stepSummary: The עולה is the exception: the תורה commands that it be skinned before it is cut up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about the עולה the תורה says: 'And he shall skin the עולה and cut it into its pieces.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי, continuing in the ברייתא, shows why the עולה does not fit the rule: its hide is taken off and separated from the meat. This sets up the next step, which explains why a פסוק is needed for its hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an עולה, the meat is burned on the מזבח but the hide is removed first. So the rule 'the hide follows the meat' cannot tell us what happens to the hide. That is why רבי said the פסוק is needed only for the עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: and he shall cut into pieces

phrases.english: But about the burnt offering it says:
"And he shall skin the burnt offering
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:6

phrases.english: and cut it into its pieces."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל עוֹלָה נֶאֱמַר בָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows why the עולה is the exception to the rule supported in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עולה is skinned and its meat is burned, so its hide does not automatically follow the meat.

steps.title: A פסוק gives the עולה's hide to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: One might think the כהנים get nothing from the עולה, so the פסוק ״עוֹר הָעֹלָה אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ teaches that the hide is theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the כהנים have no right to the hide of the עולה. So the פסוק says: 'The hide of the עולה that he offered' belongs to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's statement in the ברייתא gives the mistaken thought one might have, and then brings the פסוק that proves the hide goes to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all the meat of an עולה is burned, one might think the כהנים get nothing at all from it, not even the hide. The פסוק in ויקרא 7:8 tells us clearly that the כהן gets the hide. This is the one case where a special פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: one might think (introduces a mistaken idea)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, every hide follows its meat. The only exception is the עולה, whose hide goes to the כהנים because a פסוק says so.

phrases.english: One might think the priests would not be
entitled to its hide?
The verse teaches:
"The hide of the burnt offering that he offered."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:8

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהוּ הַכֹּהֲנִים זַכָּאִין בְּעוֹרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the פסוק needed because of the exception shown in step 13
steps.raayaObject: The כהנים get the hide of the עולה

steps.title: Which כהנים do not get the hide
steps.stepSummary: The words ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ leave out a טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים and an אונן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Shall be his' comes to leave out a טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים and an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's statement in the ברייתא learns another detail from the same פסוק: some כהנים do not get a share of the hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״לוֹ״ ('his') points only to a כהן who is fit to take part in the קרבנות. A טבול יום (who immersed today and is waiting for nightfall), a מחוסר כיפורים (who still has to bring his קרבן to finish becoming pure) and an אונן (an acute mourner) are not included.

keyTerms.meaning: someone who immersed today and stays impure until nightfall
someone who still has to bring a קרבן to finish becoming pure
an acute mourner, on the day a close relative dies

phrases.english: "Shall be his":
phrases.notes: These are the last words of the same פסוק, ויקרא 7:8.

phrases.english: to exclude one who immersed that day
and one lacking atonement, and an acute mourner.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹ יִהְיֶה – פְּרָט לִטְבוּל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Learns a further detail from the end of the same פסוק quoted in step 14
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים and an אונן do not get a share of the hides.

steps.title: Why this needs to be taught
steps.stepSummary: One might think these כהנים are kept from the meat only because it is food, and so they could still get the hide. The פסוק ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ teaches that they are left out of the hide too.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think: they don't get the meat because it is for eating, but they do get the hide because it isn't for eating. So the פסוק says 'shall be his,' to leave out a מחוסר כיפורים, a טבול יום and an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא, still in רבי's name, explains why the exclusion in the last step is needed, by showing the mistake one might make without it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These כהנים are not allowed to eat קדשים, so of course they don't get the meat. One might think that rule is only about eating, so they could still take the hide, which is not eaten. The פסוק teaches that they lose their share of the hide too, not only of the food.

keyTerms.meaning: they will acquire, get a share

steps.confusionAlert: These כהנים are left out of the hide even though a hide is not food. The rule is not only about eating. They lose their whole share.
steps.whatToRemember: A כהן who cannot eat קדשים (a טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים or an אונן) also does not get a share of the hides.

phrases.english: For one might think they don't acquire the meat
because it is for eating,
but they do acquire the hide
because it is not for eating;
so the verse teaches: "Shall be his,"
to exclude one lacking atonement,
and one who immersed that day, and an acute mourner.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁיָּכוֹל לֹא יִזְכּוּ בְּבָשָׂר – שֶׁהוּא לַאֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the exclusion in step 15 is needed
steps.raayaObject: These כהנים are left out of the hide, not only the meat

steps.title: Why doesn't the first תנא just use logic?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first תנא: why does he need the words ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ to teach that the hides of all קדשי קדשים go to the כהנים, when רבי ישמעאל shows this can be learned through a קל וחומר?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first תנא should also learn this from logic!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the first תנא needs the extra words ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ to include the hides of קדשי קדשים. It points out that רבי ישמעאל learns the same law through logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל learns through a קל וחומר from the עולה that the hides of all קדשי קדשים go to the כהנים. If logic already proves it, the first תנא's use of ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ looks unnecessary. The challenge is about the source, not about the law itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא, the first opinion quoted in a ברייתא or משנה
Let me derive it; why not learn it from
Logic; a reasoned derivation such as a קל וחומר

phrases.english: And the first tanna too,
let him derive it from logic!
phrases.notes: He means the קל וחומר רבי ישמעאל uses to give the כהנים the hides of all קדשי קדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא נָמֵי תִּיפּוֹק לִי מִדִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא ends, the גמרא challenges the first תנא's derivation in step 3, in light of רבי ישמעאל's קל וחומר in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first תנא's derivation of the hides of all קדשי קדשים from ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a קל וחומר already proves the law, a פסוק should not be needed.

steps.title: The תורה sometimes writes what logic could teach
steps.stepSummary: Even when something can be learned through a קל וחומר, the תורה sometimes takes the trouble to write it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that can be learned through a קל וחומר, the פסוק takes the trouble and writes it anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first תנא agrees the logic works. The תורה simply chose to write the law out clearly as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having a פסוק for something logic could prove is not a problem. It is a known pattern that the תורה sometimes spells out what a קל וחומר would teach. So the first תנא's פסוק and רבי ישמעאל's logic can both be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

phrases.english: A matter that comes through a kal vachomer,
the verse takes the trouble and writes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וְחוֹמֶר טָרַח וְכָתַב לַהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle of how the תורה writes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פסוק that teaches what logic proves would be extra, so the first תנא should not need one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה sometimes writes out a law even when a קל וחומר could teach it.

steps.title: What does רבי ישמעאל do with ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״?
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי ישמעאל learns the hide law from logic, the גמרא asks what he learns from the words ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל, what does he do with this ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי ישמעאל. If he does not need the פסוק for the hide, it asks what he learns from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה should teach something. Since רבי ישמעאל gets the hide law from logic, the words ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ seem to have no job in his view. The גמרא asks what they teach.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael,
this "that he has sacrificed," what does he do with it?
phrases.notes: These are the words the first תנא used for the hide (ויקרא 7:8).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הַאי אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the first תנא, the גמרא asks about רבי ישמעאל's use of the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי ישמעאל learns from ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״

steps.title: ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ leaves out three kinds of כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ to leave out a טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים and an אונן from the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to leave out a טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים and an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל learns from these words that three kinds of כהנים do not get a share in the hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ mean the hide belongs to a כהן who is fit to offer. A טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים and an אונן cannot offer, so they get no hide. This is the same law that steps 15-16 learned from ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who went to the מקוה today and waits for nightfall to be fully טהור
Someone who still needs to bring a קרבן to finish becoming טהור
A mourner on the day a close relative died

phrases.english: To exclude one who immersed that day
and one lacking atonement and an acute mourner.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּרָט לִטְבוּל יוֹם וּמְחוּסַּר כִּיפּוּרִים וְאוֹנֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי ישמעאל uses ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ to leave out a טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים and an אונן from the hide.

steps.title: Why not learn this from ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי ישמעאל could learn the exclusion of these כהנים from ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״, as the earlier ברייתא did.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him learn it from ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי ישמעאל's answer. The earlier ברייתא already learned this exclusion from ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״, so why use ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15-16 showed that ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ leaves out these three כהנים. If that phrase already teaches it, רבי ישמעאל should not need ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ for the same law. The challenge forces him to explain what ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is for.

keyTerms.meaning: "It shall be his," words in the פסוק about the כהן's share

phrases.english: But let him derive it from "shall have to himself"!
phrases.notes: That is how steps 15-16 learned it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִלוֹ יִהְיֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's use of ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ to leave out the three כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ already teaches this exclusion, so ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ is not needed for it.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל needs ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ for the bones
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ for a גזירה שוה between עולה and אשם: just as the אשם's bones are permitted, so are the עולה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל follows his own reasoning. רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is said about an עולה, and ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is said about an אשם. Just as there its bones are permitted, so too here its bones are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי ישמעאל needs ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ for a different law. He uses it to compare the עולה to the אשם about the bones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ appear about both the אשם and the עולה, so רבי ישמעאל makes a גזירה שוה. The bones of an אשם are permitted to the כהן, so the bones of an עולה are permitted too. Since ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is busy teaching this, he must use ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ for the three כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his view elsewhere
It is said here and it is said there; the opening of a גזירה שוה
Just as there, so too here

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one phrase in a פסוק can only be used for one teaching, so a תנא who uses it for one law must find another source for the other law.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael follows his own reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael:
It is said about a burnt offering "shall have to himself,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:8

phrases.english: and it is said about a guilt offering "shall have to himself";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:7

phrases.english: just as there its bones are permitted,
phrases.notes: "There" means the אשם, which the כהנים get to keep.

phrases.english: so too here its bones are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל לְטַעְמֵיהּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The phrase is needed for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is free to leave out the three כהנים, so ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי ישמעאל, ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ is used for the גזירה שוה about bones, so the exclusion must come from ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״.

steps.title: The גזירה שוה works only because the words are extra
steps.stepSummary: The words must be extra (מופני); otherwise the גזירה שוה could be broken, since an אשם's meat is permitted. But ״יִהְיֶה״ is an extra word.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words are free. For if they were not free, one could refute it: what about an אשם, whose meat is permitted to him? But ״יִהְיֶה״ is an extra word in the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a note about the גזירה שוה: it only stands because the words ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ are extra in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could argue that the אשם is different, since its meat goes to the כהן, so maybe that is why its bones are permitted too. That difference would break a normal comparison. But when the words are extra (מופני), the גזירה שוה cannot be broken by such a difference, and ״יִהְיֶה״ is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Free; extra words set aside for a גזירה שוה
One could refute it; one could point out a difference
An extra word or phrase in a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל learns the hide law from a קל וחומר, uses ״אֲשֶׁר הִקְרִיב״ to leave out a טבול יום, a מחוסר כיפורים and an אונן, and uses the extra words ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ for a גזירה שוה that the עולה's bones are permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: The question ״מָה לְאָשָׁם״ is not the גמרא's real challenge. It shows what could have broken the comparison, and the extra word ״יִהְיֶה״ is why it does not.

phrases.english: They are free;
for if they were not free, one could refute it:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְאָשָׁם שֶׁכֵּן בְּשָׂרוֹ מוּתָּר לוֹ;
phrases.english: what about a guilt offering, whose meat is permitted to him;
"shall have" is an extra word in the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּפְנֵי דְּאִי לָא מוּפְנֵי אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the גזירה שוה of step 22 holds up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה from ״לוֹ יִהְיֶה״ stands because the word ״יִהְיֶה״ is extra, so the difference between אשם and עולה cannot break it.

steps.title: The new משנה: disqualified before or after flaying
steps.stepSummary: If an offering became פסול before it was flayed, its hide does not go to the כהנים. If it became פסול after flaying, the hide does go to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Any offerings that became disqualified before they were flayed: their hides do not go to the כהנים. After they were flayed: their hides go to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a rule about who gets the hide of an offering that became disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Timing is the key. A פסול that happens before the hide is removed takes the hide down with the meat, so both are burned. Once the hide is already off, a later פסול does not take it away from the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A disqualification that makes the offering invalid
Flaying, removing the hide from the animal

phrases.english: MISHNA
All offerings that had a disqualification happen to them
phrases.notes: This means the most holy offerings, whose hides normally go to the כהנים.

phrases.english: before their flaying: their hides do not go to the priests.
After their flaying: their hides go to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים שֶׁאֵירַע בָּהֶן פְּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion of רבי ישמעאל's sources.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסול before flaying means the hide is burned. A פסול after flaying means the hide goes to the כהנים.

steps.title: רבי חנינא never saw a hide burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים reports that in all his years he never saw a hide sent out to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא, the deputy כהן גדול, said: In all my days I never saw a hide going out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: A senior כהן reports what he saw in the בית המקדש. He never saw a hide taken out to be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is testimony about practice, not a stated rule. His report suggests that hides were always given to the כהנים, even when the meat turned out to be disqualified. The next step builds a ruling from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy of the כהן גדול
The place where disqualified offerings are burned

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, the deputy of the priests, said:
In all my days I never saw
a hide going out to the place of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds eyewitness testimony to the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In his experience, a hide was never burned.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns a rule about the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא draws a rule from רבי חנינא's report: if a בכור was flayed and then found to be a טריפה, the כהנים may use its hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: From his words we learned that if someone flays a בכור and it is then found to be a טריפה, the כהנים may benefit from its hide.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא uses רבי חנינא's testimony to prove a new הלכה about a בכור that turns out to be a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal was a טריפה even before it was flayed; people just found out afterward. Normally that would make the hide burnable. But since רבי חנינא never saw a hide burned, רבי עקיבא concludes that the hide stays permitted to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn animal, given to the כהן
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said: From his words we learned
that one who flays the firstborn
and it is found to be a tereifa:
the priests may benefit from its hide.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: מִדְּבָרָיו לָמַדְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a halachic conclusion from רבי חנינא's testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hide of a בכור found to be a טריפה after flaying is permitted to the כהנים.

steps.title: The Sages reject the proof
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that 'we never saw it' does not prove anything, so the hide is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: 'We did not see' is no proof. Rather, the hide goes out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject רבי עקיבא's proof and rule the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not having seen something happen does not prove it is forbidden. Maybe the case simply never came up in רבי חנינא's time. So the regular rule applies: the animal was פסול before flaying, and the hide is burned.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We did not see,' an argument from absence

steps.whatToRemember: משנה: a פסול before flaying means the hide is burned, and after flaying it goes to the כהנים. For a בכור found to be a טריפה, רבי עקיבא permits the hide and the חכמים say it is burned.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
'We did not see' is not a proof,
rather, it goes out to the place of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין ״לֹא רָאִינוּ״ רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי עקיבא's inference.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבי חנינא's testimony and its ruling about the בכור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not having seen something is not evidence that it is forbidden.

steps.title: Whose view is the earlier משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the earlier משנה: if the altar did not acquire the meat, the כהנים do not get the hide. It notes that this applies even if the hide was flayed before the blood was sprinkled, and asks whose opinion this is.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Any offering whose meat the מזבח did not acquire, the כהנים did not acquire its hide, even if he flayed the hide before the sprinkling. Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the earlier משנה and asks which תנא it follows. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה makes no exception for a hide flayed before the זריקה. That means the hide's status depends completely on the meat. The גמרא wants to know who holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling of the blood on the altar

phrases.english: GEMARA
Any offering whose meat the altar did not acquire:
phrases.notes: This line is from the earlier משנה on 103a, about an עולה that became פסול before the blood was sprinkled.

phrases.english: the priests did not acquire its hide,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאַפְּשָׁטֵיהּ לְעוֹר קוֹדֶם זְרִיקָה.
phrases.english: even though he flayed the hide before the sprinkling.
Whose opinion is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins its discussion by asking about the earlier משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a hide flayed before זריקה still loses its status when the meat is פסול.

steps.title: It follows רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The earlier משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds that the blood does not make the hide acceptable by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון, who says: The blood does not bring acceptance for the hide by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the earlier משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, the blood works for the hide only together with the meat. If the meat is פסול, the sprinkling does nothing for the hide either, even if it was already flayed.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings acceptance, makes the offering valid

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,
who says: The blood does not bring acceptance
for the hide by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of whose view it is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who holds that the blood does not bring acceptance for the hide on its own.

steps.title: The later משנה seems to follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes our משנה, where a hide that was already flayed goes to the כהנים, and says this matches רבי. Can the first clause follow one תנא and the later clause follow another?
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the latter clause: Any offerings that became disqualified before their flaying, their hides do not go to the priests; after their flaying, their hides go to the priests. We have arrived at רבי, who says: 'The blood brings acceptance for the hide by itself.' Is the first clause רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון and the latter clause רבי?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Our new משנה seems to follow the opposite opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says that once the hide is off, a later פסול does not take it from the כהנים. That means the blood works for the hide on its own, which is רבי's view. So the earlier clause would follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and this later clause would follow רבי, and that does not seem right.
steps.confusionAlert: Here רישא means the earlier משנה on 103a, and סיפא means the משנה we just learned. They are treated as two parts of one longer משנה.

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
All offerings that had a disqualification happen to them
before their flaying: their hides do not go to the priests.
After their flaying: their hides go to the priests.
We have arrived at Rebbi, who says:
phrases.notes: רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: 'The blood brings acceptance for the hide by itself.'

phrases.aramaic: רֵישָׁא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, סֵיפָא רַבִּי?!
phrases.english: The first clause is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, and the latter clause is Rebbi?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 29 by using our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the earlier משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later clause gives the hide to the כהנים once it is flayed. This follows רבי's view that the blood works for the hide alone, so the משנה would be split between two opposing תנאים.

steps.title: אביי: The whole משנה follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the first clause also follows רבי, because רבי agrees that flaying does not happen before the blood is sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: since the later clause is רבי, the first clause is also רבי. And רבי agrees that flaying does not come before sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 30. He says the whole משנה follows one תנא, רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later clause clearly matches רבי, so אביי reads the first clause as רבי too. The first clause says the כהנים do not get the hide even if it was flayed before the blood was sprinkled. אביי explains that רבי agrees flaying does not come before sprinkling, so his rule about an already-flayed hide does not reach that case.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause (end part) of a משנה
The first clause (opening part) of a משנה
Sprinkling the blood on the altar

phrases.english: Abaye said: since the later clause is Rabbi,
the first clause is also Rabbi;

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֶה רַבִּי שֶׁאֵין הֶפְשֵׁט קוֹדֶם זְרִיקָה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi agrees that flaying does not come before sprinkling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבִּי הִיא, רֵישָׁא נָמֵי רַבִּי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 30 by placing the whole משנה under רבי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Unifying attribution: the whole משנה follows one תנא, with a qualifying admission.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause seemed to follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and to contradict רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses follow רבי. רבי agrees that flaying does not come before sprinkling, so the first clause fits his view.

steps.title: רבא: The whole משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the opposite way: the whole משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He begins to reread the phrase 'before flaying' in the later clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: since the first clause is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, the later clause is also רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. What does 'before flaying' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer, the reverse of אביי's: the whole משנה follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. His last words ask what 'before flaying' means, which sets up his rereading of the later clause in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי kept the later clause as it reads and explained the first clause to fit it. רבא keeps the first clause as it reads and must explain the later clause, which seemed to match רבי, to fit רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. To do that, he needs a new meaning for the words 'before flaying'.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: מִדְּרֵישָׁא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: Rava said: since the first clause is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא נָמֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן;
phrases.english: the later clause is also Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon;
what is meant by 'before flaying'
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, where רבא explains these words in a new way.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִדְּרֵישָׁא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, סֵיפָא נָמֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to step 30 that is the reverse of אביי's in step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Unifying attribution under the other תנא, by rereading the later clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later clause seemed to match only רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both clauses follow רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, with 'before flaying' given a new meaning (explained next).
